spans.s:
हव 1. हव, अस्, m. (fr. rt. हु), an oblation,
burnt-offering, sacrifice.
हव, अस्, अम्, m. n. calling. See 2. हव, p. 1168.

हवा हवा or हवाव, ind. (a term imply-
ing) undoubtedly, certainly.

हाव हाव, अस्, m. (fr. rt. ह्वे), calling, a
call; any feminine or coquettish gesture tending to
excite amorous sensations, blandishment, dalliance,
the airs and arts of lovers, (in these senses perhaps a
form evolved out of भाव, q. v.)
हाव, अस्, m. calling, &c. See p. 1170, col. 3.

हवङ्ग, अस्, m. (probably हवं + ग), eating
rice and curds from a metal cup.

1. हवन, अम्, n. the act of offering an oblation
with fire; an oblation to the gods, burnt-offering,
sacrifice; (ई), f. a hole made in the ground for the
sacrificial fire which is to receive a burnt-oblation.
 — 1. हवन-स्यद, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hastening to
a sacrifice.
—हवनायुस् (˚न-आय्˚), उस्, m. ‘having
the burnt-offering for its life,’ fire.

2. हवन, अम्, n. the act of calling, an invoca-
tion; challenging to battle.
—हवन-श्रुत्, त्, त्, त्,
Ved. listening to an invocation.
—२. हवन-स्यद,
अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hastening to battle.

हवनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be offered with fire, fit
for an oblation or sacrifice, sacrificial; (अम्), n. any-
thing fit for an oblation; clarified butter, ghee.

हवित्री, f. a hole made in the ground for holding
the sacred fire for an oblation.

हविष्य, अम्, n. anything fit for an oblation;
clarified butter; wild rice (or any similar wild grain);
rice mixed with ghee; a hymn in praise of oblations
(Ved).
—हविष्य-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating clarified
butter; (क्), m. fire.
—हविष्यान्न (˚य-अन्˚), अम्,
n. food fit to be eaten during certain holy days
(or during the continuance of fasts and other re-
ligious observances); any particularly pure food (as
wheat, cow's milk, &c.).
—हविष्याशिन् (˚य-आश्˚),
ई, इनी, इ, devouring clarified butter, (Manu

);
(ई), m. fire.
हविष्यन्तीय. See under हविस्.

हविस्, इस्, n. anything offered as an oblation with
fire, clarified butter, ghee; an oblation or burnt-
offering (in general); water, (in Naigh.

. enu-
merated among the उदक-नामानि); epithet of
Śiva.
—हविः-शेष, अस्, m. the residue of an obla-
tion.
—हविर्-अशन, अम्, n. the act of devouring
[]
clarified butter; (अस्), m. ‘consuming oblations,’ fire.
—हविर्-गन्धा, f. ‘smelling like clarified butter,’
the Śamī tree.
—हविर्-गेह, अम्, n. any house or
chamber in which an oblation is offered, a sacrificial
hall.
—हविर्-दा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. a giver of obla-
tions, (said of Rudra, Ṛg-veda

.)
—हविर्-
धान, अम्, n., Ved. ‘ghee-containing,’ an oblation;
(ए), n. du. the two receptacles or vehicles on which
the Soma and other offerings are put; (अस्), m., N.
of the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda

— 13
(having the patronymic Āṅgi).
—हविर्-भुज्, क्, क्,
क्, eating clarified butter; (क्), m. fire; N. of the
Pitṛs of the Kṣatriyas.
—हविर्-भू, ऊस्, f., N. of
the wife of Pulastya.
—हविर्-मथि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved.
destroying or obstructing oblations, impeding sacrificial
rites.
—हविर्-मन्थ, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= ग-
णिकारी).
—हविर्-यज्ञ, अस्, m. a particular sacrifice,
N. of the first book of the Śata-patha-Brāhmaṇa (ac-
cording to the Mādhyandina-śākhā).
—हविर्-यज्ञ-
संस्था, f. a kind of sacrifice, (seven Havir-yajña-
saṃsthās are enumerated, viz. Agny-ādheya, Agni-
hotra, Darśa-pūrṇamāsau, Cāturmāsyāni, Paśu-ban-
dha, Sautrāmaṇī, and Pāka-yajña.)
—हविर्-याजिन्,
ई, m. ‘ghee-offerer,’ a priest.
—हविष्-कृत्, त्, त्, त्,
Ved. performing a sacrifice.
—हविष्-पङ्क्ति, इस्,
m., Ved., scil. यज्ञ, a sacrifice consisting of five
oblations.
—हविष्-पति, इस्, m., Ved. the lord of a
sacrifice.
—हविष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of
oblations; (अन्तस्), m. pl., N. of a class of Pitṛs (re-
garded as progenitors of Kṣatriyas and as descended
from Aṅgiras; Manu

).
—हविष्य्-
अन्तीय, अम्, n., N. of nineteen Vedic texts begin-
ning हविष्यन्तम्, (Manu

1. हव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fit to be offered in oblations,
(Sāy. = होतव्य); (अस्), m., N. of a son of Atri;
(अम्), n. an oblation or offering to the gods (as dis-
tinguished fr. कव्य, q. v.); clarified butter, ghee.
—हव्य-कव्य, अम्, n. oblations both to the gods
and to the spirits of deceased ancestors, (also आनि, n.
pl.)
—हव्य-जुष्टि, इस्, f., Ved. the favour of an
oblation, an acceptable oblation, (Sāy. = हविः-सेवा.)
—हव्य-दाति, इस्, f., Ved. ‘oblation-giving,’ a sacri-
ficial offering; (इस्, इस्, इ), giving sacrificial offerings.
—हव्य-पाक, अस्, m. an oblation (of rice, barley,
&c.) cooked with butter and milk for presentation to
the gods; the vessel in which such an oblation is
prepared.
—हव्य-वाह्, ट्, or हव्य-वाह, अस्, m.
‘oblation-bearer,’ Agni or fire.
—हव्य-वाहन,
अस्, ई, अम्, bearing oblations, conveying oblations;
(अस्), m. fire; epithet of the ninth Kalpa; N. of a
son of Śuci.
—हव्य-वाहिनी, f. ‘oblation-bearer,’
N. of a goddess.
—हव्य-सूद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. flowing
with oblations, affording oblations (said of cows as
affording milk that yields butter for sacrificial rites).
—हव्याश (˚य-आश) or हव्याशन (˚य-अश्˚), अस्,
m. ‘oblation-eater,’ fire.

2. हव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be invoked, (Sāy.
= आह्वातव्य.)

हवस्, अस्, n., Ved. a song of praise, hymn,
prayer.

हवीमन्, आ, m., Ved. invocation; challenging;
battle, (Sāy. = सङ्ग्राम, Ṛg-veda

हावक, अस्, m. one who calls or summons; (in
nuptial ceremonies) one who summons the bride,
an attendant on the bridegroom.
